X = 15

Hence Number of men originally employed were 15.

questions.q:
Which of the two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make the given value correct?

15 + 5 - 10 × 6 ÷ 12 = 6
questions.solution:
Interchanging - and ÷

15 + 5 div 10 times 6 - 12 = 15 + frac{{5 times 6}}{{10}} - 12

15 + 3 - 12 = 6

Interchanging + and ÷

15 ÷ 5 – 10 × 6 + 12 = 3 - 60 + 12

15 – 60 ≠ 6

Interchanging + and ×

15 times 5 - 10 + 6 div 12 = 75 - 10 + (1)/(2)

65 + (1)/(2) ne 6

Interchanging + and -

15 - 5 + 10 × 6 ÷ 12 = 15 - 5 + 5

15 – 5 ≠ 6

Hence by interchanging - and ÷ we get the correct equation.

questions.q: A dealer buys an article at a discount of 20% on its list price and marks it at 25% above the list price. If he allows a 20% discount on the new list price, then his profit percent is:
questions.solution:
Let the price of the article be 100x.

Dealer bought the article at 20% discount, then

CP of the article for the dealer = 100x × [80/100] = 80x

Marked price of the article = 100x × [125/100] = 125x

SP of the article after 20% discount = 125x × [80/100] = 100x

∴ Required profit percentage = [(100x – 80x)/80x] × 100 = 25%

questions.q: The ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 7 : 5 : 8. Working together, they can complete a piece of work in 42 days. B and C worked together for 21 days and the remaining work was completed by A alone. The whole work was completed in:
questions.solution:
Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 7 : 5 : 8

Total work = 42 × (7 + 5 + 8) = 840

Work done by B and C in 21 days = (5 + 8) × 21 = 273

Remaining work = 840 – 273 = 567

Remaining work A will complete in = 567/7 = 81 days

Total time = 21 + 81 = 102 days

Net profit = [300/12000] × 100 = 2.5%

Using Allegation method

(+15) (-10)

(+2.5)

12.5 12.5

1 : 1

2 unit = 12,000

1 unit = 6,000

Now we can say cost price of 6 tables are Rs. 6,000 and cost price of 12 chairs are Rs. 6,000.

Alternate Method Sushma bought 6 tables and 12 chairs for Rs. 12,000

Let the cost of each chair & table is C & T Respectively.

6T + 12C = 12000 (i)

Now, selling price of each table = 1.15T

Now, selling price of each chair = 0.9C

Since her total gain is Rs. 300, then the total selling cost = 12000 + 300 = 12300

So,

6 × 1.15T + 12× 0.9C = 12300

6.9T + 10.8 C = 12300 (ii)

By solving the equation (i) & (ii)

T = 1000Rs, & C = 500Rs

So, total cost for table = 6T = 6×1000 = 6000Rs

questions.q: Three numbers are such that if the average of any two of them is added to the third number, the sums obtained are 164, 158 and 132 respectively. What is the average of the original three numbers?
questions.solution:
Suppose there are three number a, b and c.

According to the question

⇒ a + (b + c)/2 = 164

⇒ 2a + b + c = 164 × 2 = 328 ----(1)

⇒ b + (c + a)/2 = 158

⇒ 2b + c + a = 158 × 2 = 316 ----(2)

⇒ c + (a + b)/2 = 132

⇒ 2c + a + b = 264 ----(3)

Add equation (1), (2) and (3)

⇒ 4(a + b + c) = 908

⇒ a + b + c = 227

∴ Required average = 227/3 = 75(2)/(3)

questions.q: If x⁴ – 6x² – 1 = 0, then the value of x⁶ – 5x² + 5/x² – 1/x⁶ + 5 is:
questions.solution:
Identity Used:

(a - b)³ = a³ - b³ - 3ab (a - b)

Calculation:

x⁴ – 6x² – 1 = 0

⇒ x² – 6 – 1/x² = 0

⇒ x² – 1/x² = 6

From the above expression, we can obtain x6 – 1/x6 by using Identity mentioned above as:

⇒ (x⁶ – 1/x⁶) = (x² – 1/x²)³ + 3(x² – 1/x²)

⇒ x⁶ – 1/x⁶ = 6³ + 3 × 6 = 216 + 18 = 234

⇒ x⁶ – 5x² + 5/x² – 1/x⁶ + 5

⇒ x⁶ – 1/x⁶ – 5(x² – 1/x²) + 5

⇒ 234 – 5 × 6 + 5

⇒ 239 – 30

⇒ 20

questions.q: If a 10-digit number 1330x558y2 is divisible by 88, then the value of (x + y) is:
questions.solution:
10 digit number 1330x558y2 is divisible by 88, means number is also divisible by 11 and 8

⇒ Sum of digit of the number even place = 3 + 0 + 5 + 8 + 2 = 18

⇒ Sum of digit of the number odd place = 1 + 3 + x + 5 + y = 9 + x + y

As we know,

⇒ 9 + (x + y) – 18 = 0

⇒ x + y = 9

questions.q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She forgot lock the door when she went out in a hurry.
questions.solution:
The --She forgot lock-- part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is ---She forgot to lock--. The infinitive form of the verb --lock-- should be used.

Basically, an infinitive verb is a verb with the word to in front of it.

•

to be

•

to have

•

to hold

•

to sleep

•

to dream

When you use an infinitive verb, --to--- is a part of the verb. It is not acting as a preposition in this case. And the verb is always just the verb. It's not conjugated in any way - no -ed, no -ing, no -s on the end.

There are several possible ways to use infinitive verbs. You can use them:

•

as the subject of a sentence - To err is human; to forgive, divine.

•

like an adjective or adverb phrase that expresses purpose or intent - My instructions are to press this button every hour.

•

following an indirect object - He told me to give this to you.

•

following certain other verbs:

•

afford - We can't afford to eat out every night.

•

agree - Let's agree to disagree.

•

aim - I aim to please.

Hence the correct answer is option 1.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Lock, stock and barrel
questions.solution:
The correct answer is completely

Key Points

• Lock, stock, and the barrel is a figure of speech used predominantly in the United Kingdom and North America, meaning all, total, everything.

• The effective portions of a gun (or more specifically a musket) are the lock (used to hold ready the sparking mechanism), the stock (the portion held), and the barrel (the aiming guide and conveyor for the explosive-driven projectile). Collectively they are the whole weapon, and therefore everything.

• Example of use: *Much to his wife's surprise, he cleaned out the basement, lock, stock, and barrel.*

questions.q:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

One of the passengers was being thoroughly checked by the customs officers.
options: The customs officers thoroughly checked one of the passengers.
The customs officers were thoroughly checking one of the passengers.
The customs officers have been thoroughly checking one of the passengers.
One of the passengers was thoroughly checking the customs officers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The customs officers were thoroughly checking one of the passengers.

Key Points

• The structures for both the active and passive forms for past continuous tense are given below:

• Active form- Subject +was/were + V1 + ing + Object

• Passive form- Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Example:

• *He was playing a Cricket match. (active voice)*

• *A Cricket match was being played by him. (passive voice)*

• The given sentence is an assertive one and in the passive voice form.

• Follow the active form structure for the past continuous tense given above:

• Exchange the places of the subject and object. (One of the passengers - the custom officers)

• At last line up the remaining part

Following these steps, we finally get- *The customs officers were thoroughly checking one of the passengers.*

questions.q:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Please take these students round the biscuit factory.
options: You are requested to take these students round the biscuit factory.
Let these students to be taken round the biscuit factory.
These students should be taking round the biscuit factory.
You must take these students round the biscuit factory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "You are requested to take these students round the biscuit factory.".

Key Points

• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.

• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.

• The given sentence is in the active voice.

• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, we use the verb 'request' instead of the adverb ';please'.

• The passive format "are + V3" should be used.

• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.

• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Hence the answer is *You are requested to take these students round the biscuit factory.*

questions.q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that is crowded and noisy.
questions.solution:
The that is crowded and noisy part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is-- that are crowded and noisy. The Subject-Verb agreement rule is not followed here.

Subjects and verbs must AGREE with one another in number (singular or plural). Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural. Other places is plural, hence the verb that follows it must also be plural- --are.

the correct sentence is- Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that are crowded and noisy.

Hence the correct answer is option 2.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.

Each dancer performed very well that it was difficult to judge who the best was.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is so well that

Key Points

The underlined part of the sentence is incorrect and has to be improved.

• It should be replaced with so well that.

• The difference between SO and VERY can be a tricky question. SO and VERY are both adverbs that are used to emphasize an adjective or an adverb. In many situations, you can use either SO or VERY with no difference in meaning.

• I’m so hungry. / I’m very hungry.

• She played so well. / She played very well.

An important point to remember is: use SO, not VERY TO EMPHASIZE – 'SO…..THAT'

•

It was so windy that I couldn’t use my umbrella.

•

The English lesson was so interesting that I was surprised when it was finished.

•

The food was so good that I ate too much.

As it emphasizes the fact that all the dancers performed SO well and that is the reason why it was difficult to judge the winner.

Thus, the correct sentence is: *Each dancer performed so well that it was difficult to judge who the best was.*
